question: frac{sqrt{32} + sqrt{162}}{sqrt{18}} = ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divide each term of the numerator by the denominator: (√32 ÷ √18) + (√162 ÷ √18)

Apply rule √a ÷ √b = √(a ÷ b): √(32 ÷ 18) + √(162 ÷ 18)

Simplify fractions: √(16 ÷ 9) + √9 = 4/3 + 3

Calculate: (4 + 9) ÷ 3 = 13/3

**∴ The correct answer is 13/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: (√32 + √162) ÷ √18

Formula: √a = √(b² × c) = b√c

⇒ √32 = √(16 × 2) = 4√2

⇒ √162 = √(81 × 2) = 9√2

⇒ √18 = √(9 × 2) = 3√2

⇒ Expression = (4√2 + 9√2) ÷ 3√2

⇒ Expression = 13√2 ÷ 3√2

⇒ Answer = 13/3

**∴ The correct answer is 13/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of Surds

The square root of a product is equal to the product of the square roots: √(a × b) = √a × √b.

Quotient Rule of Surds

The square root of a quotient is equal to the quotient of the square roots: √(a ÷ b) = √a ÷ √b.

Simplifying Surds

A surd is simplified by factoring out the largest perfect square from the radicand: √50 = √(25 × 2) = 5√2.
